What is machine learning (ML)? What can an ML model do when trained properly by a scientist?

Machine learning (ML) is a way for computers to learn patterns from examples humans have identified and use those patterns to analyze new data.

Scientists have trained this model to recognize earthquake signals.

In this lesson, you will use a ML model to identify earthquakes in the same data you looked at yesterday. First, let's find an earthquake signal in the data to see how it works.

Instructions

1) In the WaveRunner, click on the box that says “Choose a station.” Scroll through the list and choose any seismograph station around Anchorage.

2) Set the "Model" dropdown to "Compact model"

3) Set the start date as November 29, 2018.

4) Set the end date as December 1, 2018.

5) In the WaveRunner's bottom control bar, click the “Run model" button.

6) In the WaveRunner's bottom control bar, click the "Timeline It!" button. An event timeline will appear below the WaveRunner, labeled “Timeline 1.”

7) Click on one of the numbered blocks above the Timeline (this will take you to the seismic event). Then click on either the “Next” or Prev” buttons to look at other labeled events.

8) Click through the Timeline and observe the different signals identified by the ML model.

9) Answer questions 1 and 2.
